title: 3rd Sitting of third session of 2025

items.text: Opening recitation (Hamd and Salawat); the sitting begins.
Roll call of members present at the sitting.
Announcement of the day's agenda (Agenda No. އޖ/3/3/2025).

Written question by Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim to Minister of Homeland Security and Technology Ali Ihusan: the ministry decided to amend the Drugs Act and run a drug prevalence study; how far have these progressed, and if not finished, why not?
Written question by Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim to Minister of Homeland Security and Technology Ali Ihusan: are there plans to identify the areas facing drug problems and to survey them?

Written question by Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim to Minister of Homeland Security and Technology Ali Ihusan: an NGO study shows rising party-drug and intravenous drug use and a risk of TB, Hepatitis B and AIDS spreading among users; does the National Drug Agency know which drugs are now used in Malé, and is there any policy or plan for this?
First reading of Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim's bill amending Law No. 4/2007 (Audit Act).
First reading of Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim's bill amending Law No. 3/2013 (Privatization, Corporatization, Monitoring and Evaluation of State Enterprises Act).
Preliminary debate on Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim's bill amending the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives.
Continued debate on the Re-employment Bill, submitted on behalf of the government by Guraidhoo MP Hanaan Mohamed Rasheed.

Continued debate on the resolution submitted by Madaveli MP Mohamed Shameez calling for the corruption flagged in the Auditor General's special audit report on Fenaka Corporation Limited to be investigated and acted on quickly.
Continued debate on Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim's bill amending Law No. 5/2009 (Land Transport Act).
Voting on items from the day's business that have reached the voting stage.

summary: The sitting put written questions on drug policy, introduced Audit Act and privatization amendments, opened debate on a constitutional amendment bill, and continued the Re-employment Bill, Fenaka resolution and Land Transport Act debates.
